canonical_title: The Exegesis of Philip K. Dick
author: Philip K. Dick (edited by Pamela Jackson and Jonathan Lethem)
card_summary: The 2011 Jackson and Lethem edition of Dick's Exegesis, the fullest published version of the roughly eight-thousand-page private journal he wrote from 1974 until his death interpreting his visionary experiences.
page_summary:
Edited by Pamela Jackson and Jonathan Lethem and published in 2011, The Exegesis of Philip K. Dick is the definitive published gathering from the enormous private journal Dick kept from 1974 to 1982. After the visionary and perceptual experiences he labeled 2-3-74, Dick spent the rest of his life writing, by hand and at typewriter, an obsessive attempt to explain what had happened to him, filling roughly eight thousand pages with theology, philosophy, autobiography, diagrams, and relentless self-revision.

The Jackson-Lethem edition selects and annotates from that mass, running to well over a thousand pages, and supplies editorial framing and notes from a range of commentators. It supersedes Sutin's 1991 In Pursuit of VALIS as the standard access point to the Exegesis, though it too remains a selection from an even larger whole.

The portal preserves two archive manifestations. This entry is the anchor for the portal's broader Exegesis resources at /exegesis and /exegesis/works, where individual strands of Dick's argument are tracked in detail.
